articles.title: A Green Spark Job Isn't Enough: Building a Fail-Closed Pipeline Health Monitor in Python
articles.excerpt: A Spark pipeline can produce the right files and still be operationally unhealthy. Maybe the Silver stage failed once and recovered. Maybe a process started but never wrote its completion event. Or pe…
articles.body: A Spark pipeline can produce the right files and still be operationally unhealthy. Maybe the Silver stage failed once and recovered. Maybe a process started but never wrote its completion event. Or perhaps a dashboard reads a half-written health report and displays a misleading green status. For a retail-media analytics pipeline, those distinctions matter: delayed campaign metrics can be mistaken for a drop in performance, while an incomplete Gold refresh can look like a successful reporting cycle. I recently added a Python-only operational monitor to my public, synthetic-data retail-media analytics pipeline . This article walks through the actual design, its event contract, failure semantics, tests, and limitations. The monitoring implementation , orchestrator , and tests are public.

articles.title: Is 'signed in' the same as 'working'? Checking a coding agent's login
articles.excerpt: A coding agent CLI can say it's signed in and still not work: the account has no plan for it, or it's out of usage until the limit resets. So in Styx, the app I'm building, 'Ready' means more than 'si…
articles.body: A coding agent CLI can say it's signed in and still not work: the account has no plan for it, or it's out of usage until the limit resets. So in Styx, the app I'm building, 'Ready' means more than 'signed in'. During setup it runs the vendor's own installer and sign-in, then sends one tiny message and waits for the answer. If the answer comes back, the plan really works. If it says 'needs a plan' or 'out of usage', the card says that in one sentence, with the fix. Two things I learned doing it. Never write your own login flow for someone else's CLI. Run their installer and their sign-in, and keep only where the binary lives and which account it reports. Passwords and tokens stay with the vendor. Some CLIs have no cheap check.

You just want to ship it, but you should write a good description. Explaining your changes, the 'why,' the 'what.' It's a mental tax I've always hated. After one particularly grueling merge week, I decided enough was enough. What if an LLM could at least draft these things for me? I wanted something that wasn't just a generic recap but actually understood the context of my changes. So, over a recent weekend, I set out to build it. Here’s how it went down: 1. Starting one in the United States is possible, but the hard part is not the smart contract. It's the institutional design: who decides what, how, and under which legal wrapper. Here's a practical checklist. This is general information, not legal advice. Talk to a US attorney experienced in digital assets before launching. 1. Define the purpose in one sentence "We fund open-source climate tools." "We collectively own and manage a creator collective." If you can't state the purpose clearly, governance will drift. 2. Decide what actually needs to be decentralized Not everything does.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 2, 2000: Expedition 1 Arrives at the International Space Station
articles.excerpt: Expedition 1 crewmates Bill Shepherd, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev pose with a model of the space station as it appeared in 2000.
articles.body: On Nov. 2, 2000, the International Space Station welcomed its first long-term residents: NASA astronaut Bill Shepherd and two Russian cosmonauts, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev. The mission was called Expedition 1. Before this expedition, NASA had launched five, one-week-long Space Shuttle missions to help build the space station and bring up supplies. But this time, the crew would be staying for four and a half months, and they weren't taking the shuttle. Instead, they took a Russian Soyuz spacecraft , and this was the first Soyuz to ever dock at the space station. During their stay at the space station, they unpacked supplies and installed new equipment, including the first solar arrays.

articles.excerpt: In this image, we can see a colorful view of an ancient, rocky Martian hill.
articles.body: In this image, we can see a colorful view of an ancient, rocky Martian hill. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UArizona) This rainbow-hued rocky plain looks like the landscape of an alien world. And, it turns out, it is. What is it? In this image, we can see an ancient, rocky hill on Mars . In the Red Planet's Southern Highlands, this alien terrain is chock-full of minerals, which we can see clearly defined in this color-enhanced view of the region. This image was snapped by the HiRISE camera aboard NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter ( MRO ), which has been studying the planet's surface, atmosphere and climate since arriving in Martian orbit in March 2006. But this isn't exactly what the surface of the planet would look like through our eyes; the image is color-enhanced.

articles.excerpt: You need a jailbroken PS5, which in turn requires firmware older than v13.60.
articles.body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority TL;DR A new open-source tool called Hydroid lets jailbroken PS5 consoles run 64-bit Android games directly without booting Linux or a virtual machine. Front ends like Playden and PC5 bring Steam access and offline PC games to the console, while the experimental EglantinePS5 emulator brings experimental Nintendo Switch 2 games. These homebrew tools require a jailbroken PS5 running older system firmware (v13.60 and below), which Sony has patched for online play. The PlayStation 5 homebrew scene has steadily transformed Sony’s flagship console into an absurdly flexible gaming rig beyond anyone’s imagination, managing everything from PS2 , PS3, Wii U, NDS, 3DS, to even Windows 7 and Nintendo Switch emulation .

articles.title: What is Starshield? A look at SpaceX's military satellite network
articles.excerpt: SpaceX is building and operating two satellite networks at the moment, Starlink and Starshield. What’s the difference between the two, and who uses them?
articles.body: SpaceX is building and operating two satellite networks at the moment, Starlink and Starshield. What’s the difference between the two, and who uses them? For more than a week in October 2026, Ukrainian drone operators found their high-speed satellite links shut off. Officials in Kyiv said that terminals for SpaceX ’s Starshield network stopped working at speeds of above 160 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour) from Oct. 14, hampering efforts to conduct defensive operations and intercept Russian drones. Full connectivity was restored on Oct. 24, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The arguments over who did what continue, but the affair highlighted how little is publicly understood about Starshield — what it is, how it relates to Starlink , and how it is operated.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
